correctness.rationale: Exact conditional Crofton normal/direction density follows from offset interval width W(theta) with integral 2(a+b). Fourier integral of absolute sine yields m_k=-(a+b exp(2ik phi))/((a+b)(4k^2-1)); independence gives T_k=|m_k|^2. With q=4p(1-p) sin^2 phi and s=sin^2 phi, A=1-q and B=1-4q(1-s); 0<q<=s<=1 is equivalent to the exact parabola and gives explicit inverse. Equality cases, endpoints, and necessity of second harmonic are proved constructively. Checker ran 20 quadratures, 1500 inverse trials, 330000 width-weighted simulated pairs and 105000 direct-hit simulated pairs. This is finite corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Literature searches and comparisons with closely relevant public geometric results did not identify the same two independent Crofton-hit line angular-harmonic inverse theorem or its parabolic feasible image. Bianchi-Gardner-Kiderlen use the spatial covariogram, Kim-Yaskin-Zvavitch direction-unlabeled projection-length distributions, Barahona Torres and coauthors an endpoint/horizontal-chord model, and the three closely relevant full published mathematical records use other measurements. The weighted-two-atom Fourier inversion has classical ancestors; residual historical-equivalence risk is explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: An old two-atom Fourier power-spectrum or Crofton-angle inversion theorem could cover the present algebra in different language; definitive priority not certified.
The 1982 chord-recognition article was only abstract-inspected; the title is relevant but its stated observable differs, and no contradiction to the current claim was identified.
Exact population moments are assumed; measurement noise could make inverse recovery unstable near degenerate parallelograms.

value.rationale: A natural motion-invariant two-line sampling experiment yields a complete algebraic inverse classification from exactly two unlabeled relative-angle observables, with sharp minimality, a full feasible-data region, and equality classes for rhombi and rectangles. The exact model has plausible uses in angular stereology and body-shape diagnostics where individual chord lengths or absolute line directions are unavailable. This is a motivated inverse-geometric classification rather than an arbitrary coordinate evaluation or numerical table.
